clue.text: Feller's warning doctor in row

indicators.note: 'in' tells us the doctor sits inside the word for a row

parts.note: a tier is a row, as of seats
MB is Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: A lumberjack's shout, apparently delivered by a doctor in an argument or a line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Feller' is one who fells trees, not a chap.
explanation.definitionFit: The cry a woodcutter gives as a tree is about to fall.

clue.text: This compiler is a fan of ranting

parts.note: the setter refers to themself as I
to rate someone is to think highly of them, be a fan

explanation.surface: The setter confesses to enjoying a good rant.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone ranting is furious, an adjective sense of angry speech.

clue.text: Party of French monarch includes a minstrel

indicators.note: 'includes' says the string of party, French word and monarch takes in the letter a

parts.note: a ball is a formal dancing party
de is French for of
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the crossword monarch

explanation.surface: A French king's party features a wandering musician.
explanation.definitionFit: A balladeer sings ballads, as a minstrel did.

clue.text: Crackers are old in pack, once more

indicators.note: crackers means crazy, so the letters of 'are old' go wild

explanation.surface: A remark that the crackers are stale, sitting in their packet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pack, once more' is a verb: to charge a gun or fill something again.
explanation.definitionFit: To reload is to pack or load again, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Throw mud at Oscar in sloppy mudbath

indicators.note: 'in' places the Oscar letter among the shuffled letters
something sloppy is messy, so the letters of mudbath are jumbled

parts.note: Oscar is O in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone flings mud at an Academy Award winner wallowing in a muddy bath.
explanation.definitionFit: To throw mud at someone is to slander or criticise them, which is the verb meant.

clue.text: Old copper arch, way above jogger

indicators.note: in a down clue, 'above' puts the arch and way on top of the jogger

parts.note: a bow is an arch shape
a street is a way or road
a runner is one who jogs

explanation.surface: A retired policeman, an arch and a road above a jogger, like a scene description.
explanation.walkthrough: The Bow Street Runners were London's first professional police force, from the 18th century, based at Bow Street magistrates' court.
explanation.definitionFit: These were early London police officers, so a historical policeman, copper being slang.

clue.text: Taunting upset father in disreputable bar

indicators.note: 'in' sets the upturned father inside the seedy bar

parts.note: a dive is a seedy drinking place

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: to sire is to father; a sire is a father

explanation.surface: Mocking a distressed dad in a seedy bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' looks like distressed, describing the father, but it is the signal to turn him over.
explanation.definitionFit: Derisive remarks mock and jeer, just as taunting ones do.

clue.text: Best known hairstyle

parts.note: a secret that is out is known
a do (hairdo) is a hairstyle

explanation.surface: A notable hairdo, the finest one about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Best' is a verb here, to beat.
explanation.definitionFit: To best someone is to surpass or beat them, a verb synonym.

clue.text: High-quality vase lifted fine, not heavy

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifted means raised up, so the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a pot is a vessel like a vase
F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine
light means not heavy

explanation.surface: A precious vase raised up turns out fine and surprisingly light.
explanation.definitionFit: Top-flight means of the first rank, excellent.

clue.text: With everyone loud, humble one's sidelined

parts.note: all means everyone
f, forte, is the musical mark for loud
to humble someone is to lower them

explanation.surface: Among a noisy crowd, a modest person is left out.
explanation.definitionFit: A wallflower is a shy person left at the edge of a dance or party, ignored.

clue.text: Model seen among pretty people

indicators.note: the letters are seen among the words, running across the gap

explanation.surface: A fashion model spotted among the beautiful people.
explanation.definitionFit: A type is a model or standard example, as in a prototype.

clue.text: Group leave after area is reserved

indicators.note: 'after' places the leave word behind the area letter

parts.note: a set is a group
to part is to leave or go away

explanation.surface: A band quits after the stage space is booked.
explanation.definitionFit: Something set apart is reserved or kept aside for a special purpose.

clue.text: Pampered pet's first painting framed by good person

indicators.note: framed by means surrounded, so the saint's letters go round the rest

parts.note: ST, saint, is a good person

indicators.note: first picks the opening letter of the word pet's

parts.note: an oil is an oil painting

explanation.surface: A spoilt animal's first portrait, framed by a kindly owner.
explanation.definitionFit: A spoilt child or pet has been overindulged, which is to say pampered.

clue.text: Frenchman dropping off one Monsieur chez nous?

indicators.note: dropping off means losing, so one letter is removed

parts.note: homme is French for man
M is the abbreviation of Monsieur, and one of the two is lost

explanation.surface: A Frenchman nodding off at a gentleman's house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropping off' looks like falling asleep but signals removal of one M from HOMME.
explanation.definitionFit: Chez nous is French for at our house, our dwelling place, so the question mark flags a definition by example.

clue.text: Played grave role in Titanic

indicators.note: the letters of 'grave role' are played with, rearranged

explanation.surface: An actor took a solemn part in the film Titanic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Titanic' looks like the film or ship but is the adjective, huge.
explanation.definitionFit: Titanic means enormous, which is excessively big.

clue.text: See veins damaged with advance in years

indicators.note: damaged veins are broken, so their letters are rearranged

parts.note: to age is to grow older

explanation.surface: Noticing veins harmed as one grows older.
explanation.definitionFit: To envisage is to picture or foresee, to see in the mind's eye.

clue.text: Strong drink consumed by son and daughter quickly

indicators.note: the drink is swallowed by, so sits inside, the son and daughter letters

parts.note: tea is a drink
fast means quickly

explanation.surface: The children gulp down a stiff drink in a hurry.
explanation.definitionFit: Steadfast means firm and unwavering, strong in loyalty or resolve.

clue.text: Part of shoe gashed — that's a blow

parts.note: the upper is the top part of a shoe
gashed means cut

explanation.surface: A sliced shoe is a disappointment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a blow' sounds like bad news but is a punch.
explanation.definitionFit: An uppercut is a rising punch, a type of blow in boxing.

clue.text: Order unfinished, bed is rickety

indicators.note: unfinished means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: a decree is an order
the pit is slang for bed

explanation.surface: An order left incomplete because the bed is wobbly.
explanation.definitionFit: Decrepit means worn out by age, shaky, as rickety furniture is.

clue.text: Grazes perhaps from saddle after cycling

indicators.note: cycling moves the first letter to the end

parts.note: a saddle is a seat

explanation.surface: Skin grazes, perhaps, from a bike saddle after a ride.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grazes' looks like scrapes but means feeds, as cattle do; 'cycling' moves S from the front of SEAT to the back.
explanation.definitionFit: Grazing is one way an animal feeds, hence perhaps.

clue.text: Male team in green representing this country?

indicators.note: 'in' tells us the team goes inside the green word

parts.note: eco means environmentally green
XI, eleven, is a team in football or cricket

explanation.surface: A men's side in green kit, which nation is it?
explanation.definitionFit: Mexico is a nation, and its football side does play in green, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Pester power contrary local girl used regularly

indicators.note: contrary means turned the other way, so the girl word reads backwards

parts.note: gal is a dialect or colloquial word for girl

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter of the word

explanation.surface: A contrary local girl uses pester power, nagging until she gets her way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contrary' turns GAL to LAG; 'regularly' takes U and E from 'used'. Pester power is children nagging parents to buy things.
explanation.definitionFit: To plague someone is to harass or keep bothering them.

clue.text: Tory MP shielding head from liquid put protective wear on

indicators.note: shielding means covering, so the Tory MP's name goes round the letter

parts.note: Michael Gove was a Conservative (Tory) MP and minister

indicators.note: head from takes the first letter of liquid

explanation.surface: A Conservative politician donning protective clothing against a hazardous liquid.
explanation.definitionFit: To glove a hand is to cover it with protective handwear.

clue.text: Constant name appearing three times in travelling guide

indicators.note: travelling means moving about, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: N is the abbreviation for name, here taken three times

explanation.surface: A tour guide who keeps repeating a name.
explanation.walkthrough: Three Ns mix with GUIDE under 'travelling'.
explanation.definitionFit: Unending means never stopping, perpetual, which is constant.

clue.text: Sounds from TV playing up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means read from the bottom, so backwards

parts.note: a TV playing is a set on

explanation.surface: Noises from a television that is malfunctioning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing up' looks like misbehaving; 'up' reverses SET ON.
explanation.definitionFit: Notes are musical sounds.

clue.text: Group excursion almost over

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter goes

parts.note: a trip is an excursion
O is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: A party's outing nearly finished.
explanation.definitionFit: A trio is a group of three, an example of a group.

clue.text: Trusted female prisoner if backed by Italian poet

parts.note: a con is a convict, a prisoner

indicators.note: backed means turned back to front, so the little word if reads backwards

parts.note: Dante Alighieri, author of the Divine Comedy

explanation.surface: A trusted woman inmate, should Dante support her.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backed' reverses IF to FI; 'by' simply links it to the poet.
explanation.definitionFit: A confidante is a woman to whom secrets are entrusted.

clue.text: Holding spear oddly, hinder renegade

indicators.note: holding means containing, so the hinder word holds the picked letters

parts.note: to deter is to hinder or discourage

indicators.note: oddly takes the odd-numbered letters of spear

explanation.surface: Clutching a spear strangely, someone blocks a turncoat.
explanation.definitionFit: A deserter abandons their side, a turncoat or renegade.

clue.text: Dull books about British milk

indicators.note: about means around, so the books letters surround the British letter

parts.note: OT, Old Testament, is a set of books of the Bible
to milk something is to exploit or use it

explanation.surface: Boring books about British dairy.
explanation.definitionFit: Obtuse means slow-witted, dull of mind.
